pr_comments: I have not looked at the issue, but the current releases of ada do not use ICU (at all). In fact, ada has no dependency.

I think reverting is not the fix for this. ICU based `toASCII` method has a lenient mode which is passed as a second argument to `toASCII` method, which `ada::idna` does not have. We are currently investigating it with @lemire https://github.com/ada-url/idna/pull/32
I opened a backport to fix this @aduh95 https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/48873

issue_context.title: URL.parse fails on URLs with comma separated hosts
issue_context.body:
### Version

v18.17.0

### Platform

Linux XXXXX 5.4.0-137-generic #154-Ubuntu SMP Thu Jan 5 17:03:22 UTC 2023 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Subsystem

_No response_

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

Parsing URL's with comma separated hosts throws a _TypeError [ERR_INVALID_URL]: Invalid URL_ error. This URL parsed correctly in in node v18.16.1.

```
const URL = require('url');
URL.parse("mongodb://127.0.0.1,127.0.0.2:27017")
```


### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

Always.

### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior?

URL parsed rather than exception thrown.

### What do you see instead?

An exception is thrown.

### Additional information

This is a serious problem because such URL's are used reguarly when configuring eg DB connections which now fail. This is the case with the MongoDB driver for instance.
comments:
With node v18.17.0,  Ada 2.5.0 is delivered and we have the same issue.

We noticed that in node v20.4.0 , Ada 2.5.1 is delivered and there we dont have the issue.

Maybe it is possible to update also to Ada 2.5.1 in node v18.17.1 or something?
I don't think it is related to Ada? AFAIK `url.parse()` is the legacy URL parser.

`url.parse` calls `toASCII` method which is implemented under `ada::idna::to_ascii`. `to_ascii` returns an empty string if the value is invalid. In this particular case, we are receiving an empty string, which may be caused by this. Investigating it under: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/48855
strange that it doesnt cause problems under ada 2.5.1 🙈

> With node v18.17.0, Ada 2.5.0 is delivered and we have the same issue.
> 
> We noticed that in node v20.4.0 , Ada 2.5.1 is delivered and there we dont have the issue.
> 
> Maybe it is possible to update also to Ada 2.5.1 in node v18.17.1 or something?

Still happening in v18.17.1, any plan to fix it?
It is fixed at https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/48873 and will be released in the next Node 18 release.
